tokyo_kanmi_mitsuya.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop has a bilingual first-party site and it is deliberately minimal: hours (12:00–17:00, last orders 16:30, 完売次第終了 — closing when sold out), the address 台東区浅草1-32-13, a phone number, and the instruction 「お問い合わせはインスタグラムのメッセージからお願いします」 — enquiries by Instagram message. A /menu/ path returns 404. There is no board published anywhere on the site. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WORTH A RE-CHECK RATHER THAN A SHRUG, BECAUSE OF WHAT IT IS. 甘味 shops are the best dessert format in Japan for both diets — the 甘味処 西山 record elsewhere in this set shows why: 寒天 (agar, from seaweed), あんこ (azuki and sugar), 白玉 (glutinous RICE flour) and 黒蜜 are all plant and all wheat-free, so anmitsu, mamekan and zenzai are routinely safe on both counts where nothing else on a Japanese menu is. A kanmi counter that sells out daily is exactly the kind of place worth the phone call. But nothing about THIS shop’s bowls is published, and the general shape of the category is not evidence about this kitchen — so no items are recorded. Ask on Instagram, or re-check when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_tsukemen_gonokami_seisak.price_note: Complete card from the operator’s own page for this specific branch (株式会社五ノ神製作所 keeps one page per shop; this is 新宿, 渋谷区千駄ヶ谷5-33-16, 11:00-21:30 with last order 21:00, open daily). The shop describes itself as an 海老つけ麺専門店 — a prawn-tsukemen specialist — and says the Shinjuku bowls push the prawn flavour harder than the 本店 does. Bilingual JP/EN names as printed. ⚠ TSUKEMEN IS THE WORST-CASE STRUCTURE FOR A COELIAC AND THIS SHOP ADDS A SECOND PROBLEM ON TOP. The noodle is wheat; the dipping broth is a reduced prawn-shell soup which in this genre is finished with soy tare; and 海老 (prawn) is itself one of Japan’s eight major allergens, so this is a shop a shellfish-allergic diner should skip entirely rather than negotiate. No allergen statement is published. ⚠ THE SIDE DISHES ARE NOT AN ESCAPE ROUTE: ご飯 at 150 yen is plain rice, but the 海老味たまごかけご飯 is TKG built on the same prawn tare, バジルご飯 carries a basil sauce of unpublished composition, and 焼チーズ飯 is grilled cheese. The toppings 味玉 and 三角メンマ are both soy-marinated, and チャーシュー is soy-braised. The only two items on this card with no obvious wheat route are the heaped cabbage and the mozzarella.

This is a course-only French bistro: NOT ONE À-LA-CARTE DISH IS PUBLISHED, only the course skeletons — 前菜 / スープ / 魚料理 / 肉料理 / パン2個 / デザート / 珈琲 or 紅茶 — so no individual dish name or diet flag can honestly be recorded. What is recorded is every course and its price, plus the à-la-carte supplements, which are the only single items the shop prices. ⚠ EVERY COURSE ON BOTH CARDS INCLUDES パン2個 AS A FIXED COMPONENT — two bread rolls are built into the price, not offered — so wheat is on the table by default at every seat, and the supplements list 自家製パン at 150 yen a piece and butter at 75 yen, confirming the bread is house-baked. A French bistro kitchen is a roux, flour-dusting and beurre-manié kitchen; nothing here is published about allergens, and the fish and meat dishes are 本日の (chef’s daily choice) so they cannot be checked ahead. ⚠ THE SITE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON LUNCH HOURS: the lunch MENU page heads the card 11:30～14:30 (L.o.12:30) while the shop-information block on the same page says ランチ 11:30～15:00 (14:00 L.o). Both are recorded as printed; ring to confirm. Dinner is 17:30-22:30 (21:30 L.o) per the info block and 17:30-21:30 (L.o.20:00) per the dinner card. tokyo_korakuen_hanten.price_note: The hotel publishes four dated PDF menus — a numbered 73-item grand à la carte plus lunch, dinner and common course cards, the seasonal ones marked 2026.9.1 - 11.30 — and every price is footed 「表示料金はサービス料・消費税込みの料金です」, service charge and tax included, which is unusual and worth trusting. 後楽園飯店 is the Cantonese-Sichuan dining room of the 東京ドームホテル. The course cards note メニューは変更になる場合がございます. ⚠ THE STRUCTURAL POINT THAT MAKES A CHINESE BANQUET ROOM DIFFERENT FROM A WESTERN ONE, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. The あんかけ sauces that cover a third of this menu are thickened with 片栗粉, potato starch — NOT with a wheat roux the way a Japanese or French kitchen would do it. So the thickener itself is not the problem here, which is the opposite of the demi-glace and curry-roux situation elsewhere in this dataset. The problem is what the sauce is FLAVOURED with, and in this kitchen that is 醤油, 蠔油 oyster sauce, 豆板醤 and 甜麺醤 — and 甜麺醤 is a wheat-flour paste by definition while 豆板醤 is conventionally wheat-fermented. A starch-thickened sauce built on those is still a wheat sauce. ⚠ SO THE COELIAC ANSWER IS NO ACROSS ALMOST THE ENTIRE CARD, AND THE FEW EXCEPTIONS ARE WORTH NAMING PRECISELY. 麻婆豆腐(四川風) at ￥1,950 and 麻婆茄子 at ￥1,950 are doubanjiang dishes; 回鍋肉 (豚肉とキャベツの味噌炒め) at ￥2,350 names 味噌 and is a tianmianjiang dish; every 炒麺 and 湯麺 is a wheat noodle; and the entire 点心 section — 水餃子, 焼売, 蒸し餃子, 小籠包, 春巻, 花巻, 桃饅頭 — is wheat wrappers and steamed wheat buns. ⚠ WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH ASKING ABOUT, IN ORDER. 胡麻団子 at ￥900 is glutinous rice flour and sesame with no wheat in its definition — but it is deep-fried in the same oil as the 春巻, whose pastry is wheat, so the fryer is the question. 杏仁豆腐 at ￥750 is almond and milk set with agar or gelatin and is the cleanest sweet on the card. ピータン at ￥2,100 is a century egg, 野菜の甘酢漬け at ￥1,950 is a vinegar pickle, and ライス at ￥400 is plain rice. 青菜の塩味炒め ガーリック風味 at ￥2,100 is the one green dish built on salt and garlic rather than soy — the single most promising savoury plate here, and still an ask, because Chinese salt stir-fries are routinely finished with 紹興酒 and a chicken 湯. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN THIS ROOM IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS, AND THE REASON IS THE STOCK RATHER THAN THE INGREDIENTS. 麻婆茄子, 白麻婆豆腐, 青菜の塩味炒め and 野菜スープ all read as plant dishes, but Chinese banquet kitchens build essentially everything on a 湯 made from chicken and pork, and the shop declares nothing. 野菜のオイスターソース煮込み at ￥2,450 names oyster sauce outright, so that one is settled. ⚠ TWO OTHER THINGS TO KNOW. The 白麻婆豆腐 at ￥1,950 is a white mapo, which in most kitchens means no doubanjiang — it is the mapo to ask about rather than the red one, and the dinner course offers 赤麻婆、白麻婆の二種味くらべ so both are made here. And the shark-fin dishes run from ￥2,150 a portion up to ￥14,000 for the 姿煮; the courses are 全家楽 family lunch ￥7,000, weekday ランチセット ￥3,500, prix-fixe dinner ￥8,700, 舞扇 ￥8,500 (with free drinks ￥10,500) and 華扇 ￥10,000 (with free drinks ￥12,000).

The shop states it works with 鳥取産「匠の大山鶏」and「美桜鶏」 chicken, and that the day's buying can change what is on. ⚠ THE ONE THING THE BOARD DOES NOT SAY IS THE ONE THING A COELIAC NEEDS. Yakitori is served either 塩 (salt) or タレ (a soy-based basting sauce), and this board names neither for any skewer. Soy sauce is wheat by default, so every unmarked skewer is an ASK — the answer at a counter like this is usually 'salt is fine', but nothing published confirms it. Items whose name carries the seasoning (味噌漬, ポン酢, 明太子, 茶漬け, にゅうめん, 雑炊, 焼きおにぎり) are marked wheat outright rather than left open. ⚠ AND にゅうめん IS SOMEN — WHEAT NOODLES — sitting in the 〆 block between two rice dishes, which is exactly where it will be missed.

tokyo_tencups.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE SITE SERVES NO CONTENT TO ANYTHING THAT IS NOT A BROWSER RUNNING JAVASCRIPT. tencupsjp.com returns 200 and about 200 kB of HTML, and the only human-readable string in the whole document is the og:title, 'TENCUPS HOME'. There is no server-rendered body, no navigation, no dish, no price and no address; the generator meta is 'export_website', i.e. a site exported from a visual builder that hydrates entirely on the client. It was tried twice — once with curl and a desktop user agent, once through a renderer — and neither produced a menu. ⚠ THE HTML DOES CONTAIN A FEW FRAGMENTS OF UNRELATED JAPANESE PROSE about a music-news媒体 (「最新の音楽ニュース」, 「ミュージシャンの音楽的ルーツ」, and what look like band names), which is either a stray embedded widget or a sign that the domain now carries something other than the café. THAT AMBIGUITY IS THE REASON THIS RECORD IS CONFIDENCE MEDIUM RATHER THAN HIGH: it is not certain that this URL still belongs to the shop, and it would be wrong to attribute anything found on it to TENCUPS.
